subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: The Escalator: Moving Stairs
description: One-minute skill: The Escalator: Moving Stairs.

hook.text: Escalator steps appear and vanish. They flatten at the top, loop underneath, and reform at the bottom.

buildup.text: A chain loop carries step modules. Each step has wheels that ride two separate tracks at different heights.

discovery.text: One track guides the step wheels, another guides the riser wheels. The height difference creates the step shape.

twist.text: At the landing, both tracks converge to the same height. The steps flatten and slide into a comb plate.

climax.text: An escalator combines chains, gears, motors, tracks, and cams. It's a factory of moving parts you stand on.

punchline.text: The stairs move. You don't. Engineering at its most generous.

quiz.question: How do escalator steps flatten at the top and bottom?
options: Hydraulic pistons push each step flat as it reaches the landing
Two separate tracks converge, bringing step and riser wheels to the same height
Springs inside each step automatically retract the risers
